items.title: FDA approves Abbott's Amplatzer Paraclose, which the company calls the first US transcatheter device designed to close paravalvular leaks around surgical valves
items.summary: On Oct 28, 2026, Abbott announced FDA approval of the Amplatzer Paraclose PVL Occluder, which it describes as the first and only US-approved transcatheter device specifically designed to close paravalvular leak (PVL) around surgical replacement heart valves, as an alternative to repeat open-heart surgery.
bullets: What it is: an oblong (elliptical) occluder delivered by catheter through a leg artery or vein and placed within the leak to close it; sold outside the US as the Amplatzer Valvular Plug III, approved in Europe since 2020.

Why it matters: PVL occurs in about 7-17% of mitral and 5-10% of aortic valve replacements and can cause heart failure symptoms and haemolytic anaemia; Abbott says US physicians previously had no approved alternative to repeat open-heart surgery.
Evidence: approval was based on PARADIGM, a prospective, multicentre, single-arm study of 200 patients; the press release does not report the efficacy or safety figures.
Scope: the US label covers PVL around surgical replacement valves; the announcement does not mention leaks after TAVI.
Caveat: single-arm data with no randomised comparison to surgery; full PARADIGM results should be read when published.
